config.design: Independent extension on twelve prospectively fixed new cases. Same five-project service desk, same duty-lead question. Fresh Astra, Sol and Fable originals were generated from identical terse facts through their subscription CLIs. Unlike the earlier paired approvals, every held alternative is an independently generated first-proposal draft and the active lead leaves a second status artifact. Both answer orders, both modalities and every case are included.

files.A/cases/241/intake.txt: campus debate | afternoon heat alarm in hall 2 | backup hall holds 90 | 110 attendees registered | 15 plan to join remotely | sound check in 25 minutes | facilities reassessment pending
files.A/work/479.txt: Hold admission to Hall 2 while Facilities reassesses the afternoon heat alarm. Prepare the backup hall and ask for five more remote volunteers. With 110 registered and 15 planning to join remotely, we expect 95 in person. Use the backup only if the in-person count is confirmed at 90 or fewer. If Facilities clears Hall 2, use it. Recheck before sound check in 25 minutes.
files.A/work/194.txt: Move the debate to the backup hall now and relocate the sound check there in 25 minutes. Assuming the 15 remote participants are among the 110 registered, about 95 would attend in person, five over the 90 capacity, so cap entry at 90 and offer the remote link to the overflow. Return to hall 2 only if facilities clears the heat alarm in writing before sound check, or if in-person numbers are confirmed far above 90.
files.A/work/128.txt: The campus debate is moving out of Hall 2 because of a heat alarm there this afternoon. Please go to the backup hall instead. It seats 90, which is slightly fewer than we expect in person, so entry is first come, first served, and we ask anyone who can join remotely to do so. If facilities clears Hall 2 in time, we will post an update.
files.A/work/270.txt: Campus debate venue decision pending following the afternoon heat alarm in Hall 2. Facilities reassessment is outstanding. Of 110 registrants, 15 plan to attend remotely, leaving 95 expected on site. The backup hall holds 90, a shortfall of five places. Admission to Hall 2 is on hold. The next decision point is before sound check, due in 25 minutes.

files.A/work/208.txt: Before 09:00 prep, hold everything in that fridge and probe the back shelf and a few items' core temperatures with the calibrated probe. The display reads 9 °C but the front probed at 4 °C, and the 05:10 door alarm means we can't yet tell how warm stock got or for how long. If all readings are 5 °C or below, release the food and log a sensor fault. If anything reads above 8 °C, discard high-risk items and switch menu.
files.A/work/345.txt: Before 09:00, put the fridge’s perishable food on hold and use stock from a verified cold unit for lunch prep. The 4 °C front reading doesn’t clear the back shelf, and the 05:10 door alarm doesn’t tell us how long food may have been warm. Check food temperatures at the front and back with a calibrated probe and review the overnight log. Release held food only if the readings and time history meet the school’s food-safety limits.
files.A/work/302.txt: The school kitchen fridge door alarm went off at 05:10. The display reads 9 °C, but an independent probe measured 4 °C at the front. The back shelf hasn’t been checked, and we don’t yet know how long food may have been above a safe temperature. For 09:00 lunch prep, don’t use food from this fridge until the kitchen lead checks food temperatures throughout and reviews the temperature records. Use ingredients from verified safe storage or switch to the backup menu.

files.A/work/698.txt: Before the deadline, close the north manual shutoff and check whether the meter stops. The north meter rose overnight with its timer off while the south meter stayed steady, so check for a leak or unexpected flow on the north line. Let garden staff know the shutoff may also stop the fountain. If the fountain’s normal operation accounts for the full increase, reopen the valve. If the meter keeps rising with the valve closed, call maintenance to check upstream.
files.A/work/596.txt: Before the deadline, check whether the fountain is drawing water. If it can be paused safely, pause it and recheck the north meter. If the meter still rises, close the manual shutoff and flag the possible leak for repair; note that the fountain will lose water too. The north timer is off and the south meter is stable. If normal fountain use accounts for the rise, leave the shared pipe open.
files.A/work/587.txt: The north irrigation meter has been rising overnight even though the north timer is off; the south meter is stable. We haven't found the cause yet. The north line shares a pipe with the fountain, so the fountain or a leak may be responsible. For now, please leave the north timer off, water north beds by hand from the south side, and report any wet ground or pooling. We'll close the manual shutoff tonight to test, so the fountain may be off.

files.A/work/563.txt:
Before the morning rush, trust the rack, not the kiosk. Have someone move bikes from the nearly full neighboring rack to this one, then correct the kiosk count to match what is physically docked.

The kiosk says 14 and the rack holds 5. With the last truck manifest unsigned, nothing confirms that the delivery happened, and commuters will arrive expecting bikes that aren't there.

Change course if the driver confirms a drop-off or a recount finds the missing nine.
files.A/work/422.txt: Before the morning rush, have someone count the bikes at the rack and check that they’re usable. Don’t send a truck based on the kiosk reading: 14 bikes can’t fit in five spaces, and the unsigned manifest doesn’t confirm a delivery. Update the kiosk with the verified count. If the check shows too few usable bikes for commuters, move bikes from the nearly full neighboring rack, but only into confirmed open spaces.
files.A/work/219.txt: The bike-share kiosk shows 14 bikes available, but only 5 are at the rack. The last truck manifest is unsigned, so we can’t confirm whether the delivery was completed. If you’re heading out this morning, don’t count on the kiosk total; have a backup if you need to leave on time. If you’re returning a bike, the neighboring rack is nearly full, so check for an open dock or plan to use another station.

files.A/work/541.txt: Before the deadline, close the north manual shutoff and check whether the meter stops. The north meter rose overnight with its timer off while the south meter stayed steady, so check for a leak or unexpected flow on the north line. Let garden staff know the shutoff may also stop the fountain. If the fountain’s normal operation accounts for the full increase, reopen the valve. If the meter keeps rising with the valve closed, call maintenance to check upstream.
files.A/work/957.txt: Before the deadline, check whether the fountain is drawing water. If it can be paused safely, pause it and recheck the north meter. If the meter still rises, close the manual shutoff and flag the possible leak for repair; note that the fountain will lose water too. The north timer is off and the south meter is stable. If normal fountain use accounts for the rise, leave the shared pipe open.
files.A/work/969.txt: The north irrigation meter has been rising overnight even though the north timer is off; the south meter is stable. We haven't found the cause yet. The north line shares a pipe with the fountain, so the fountain or a leak may be responsible. For now, please leave the north timer off, water north beds by hand from the south side, and report any wet ground or pooling. We'll close the manual shutoff tonight to test, so the fountain may be off.

files.A/work/465.txt: Test the backup cable now, while there's still time to recover if it fails. The laptop plays captions fine, so the fault is likely in the cable or the projector's processing; a swap is the fastest way to tell which. If lag persists, switch the projector to game or low-latency mode. With 30 reserved, I'd hold doors rather than screen with bad captions. Laptop playback is fine, but the audience needs readable, correctly timed captions on the big screen. If the lag persists or returns, notify the 30 ticket holders before doors open and offer a later screening or refund rather than start with a known caption problem.
files.A/work/946.txt: Quick update for tonight’s community cinema screening: The captions are in sync on the laptop but lag on the projector. Please keep your reservation for now and check this thread before heading out, especially if you rely on captions. We’ll post another update before doors open.
